mx.teacher_note: All breathing animals inhale by moving their ribs up and out and their diaphragm down.

intelligence.enrichment: During inhalation, the ribs move up and outwards and the diaphragm moves down, increasing space in the chest so air is drawn in; during exhalation, the diaphragm moves upward, the ribs move back, and air is forced out. rib and diaphragm movement changes chest space -> air moves into or out of the lungs The learner correctly applies this rule: During inhalation, the ribs move up and outwards and the diaphragm moves down, increasing space in the chest so air is drawn in; during exhalation, the diaphragm moves upward, the ribs move back, and air is forced out. Breathing in and out happens because air chooses to move, not because the chest space changes.
